From fdfaf64e75397567257e1051931f9a3377360665 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@plumgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2014 15:56:51 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] x86: bpf_jit: support negative offsets

Commit a998d4342337 claimed to introduce negative offset support to x86 jit,
but it couldn't be working, since at the time of the execution
of LD+ABS or LD+IND instructions via call into
bpf_internal_load_pointer_neg_helper() the %edx (3rd argument of this func)
had junk value instead of access size in bytes (1 or 2 or 4).

Store size into %edx instead of %ecx (what original commit intended to do)

Fixes: a998d4342337 ("bpf jit: Let the x86 jit handle negative offsets")
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@plumgrid.com>
Cc: Jan Seiffert <kaffeemonster@googlemail.com>
Cc: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Acked-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/arch/x86/net/bpf_jit.S b/arch/x86/net/bpf_jit.S
index 877b9a1b2152..01495755701b 100644
--- a/arch/x86/net/bpf_jit.S
+++ b/arch/x86/net/bpf_jit.S
@@ -140,7 +140,7 @@ bpf_slow_path_byte_msh:
 	push	%r9;						\
 	push	SKBDATA;					\
 /* rsi already has offset */					\
-	mov	$SIZE,%ecx;	/* size */			\
+	mov	$SIZE,%edx;	/* size */			\
 	call	bpf_internal_load_pointer_neg_helper;		\
 	test	%rax,%rax;					\
 	pop	SKBDATA;					\
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/net/bpf_jit.S`**
   - The line that moves the size into the register has been modified:
     - Changed from `mov $SIZE,%ecx;` to `mov $SIZE,%edx;`
   - This change ensures that the size of the data being accessed is correctly passed to the `bpf_internal_load_pointer_neg_helper()` function in the `%edx` register instead of `%ecx`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `bpf_jit.S` directly addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (a998d4342337) that claimed to support negative offsets in the x86 JIT compilation for BPF. The original implementation incorrectly stored the size in the `%ecx` register, leading to the third argument of the helper function containing an invalid value. By moving the size to `%edx`, the patch corrects this oversight, ensuring that the helper function receives the correct access size, thereby fixing the negative offset support functionality.

Here is the commit message:
x86: bpf_jit: support negative offsets

Commit a998d4342337 claimed to introduce negative offset support to x86 jit,
but it couldn't be working, since at the time of the execution
of LD+ABS or LD+IND instructions via call into
bpf_internal_load_pointer_neg_helper() the %edx (3rd argument of this func)
had junk value instead of access size in bytes (1 or 2 or 4).

Store size into %edx instead of %ecx (what original commit intended to do)

Fixes: a998d4342337 ("bpf jit: Let the x86 jit handle negative offsets")
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@plumgrid.com>
Cc: Jan Seiffert <kaffeemonster@googlemail.com>
Cc: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Acked-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect assignment of the size of the data being accessed to the `%ecx` register instead of the `%edx` register when calling the `bpf_internal_load_pointer_neg_helper()` function. This resulted in the third argument of the function containing an invalid (junk) value, which led to improper handling of negative offsets in the x86 JIT compilation for BPF.

The size of the data being accessed was incorrectly assigned to the `%ecx` register instead of the `%edx` register. This caused the third argument of the `bpf_internal_load_pointer_neg_helper()` function to contain a junk value, leading to improper handling of negative offsets during execution.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
